name: Ye Lang Disco (野狼disco)
blurb: Gem's 2019 disco-rap hit, famous on Douyin for its "draw a dragon" hand dance
title: Ye Lang Disco (野狼disco) by Gem: Why It Went Viral on Douyin
description: 野狼disco (Wild Wolf Disco) is a 2019 song written and sung by Changchun rapper 宝石Gem (Dong Baoshi). Its "draw a dragon" hand dance swept Douyin.
h1: Why did "Ye Lang Disco" (野狼disco) go viral?
answer: 野狼disco (Yě Láng Disco, "Wild Wolf Disco") is a song written, composed and performed by 宝石Gem (Gem, real name 董宝石 Dong Baoshi), a rapper from Changchun in northeast China, released digitally on 2 September 2019. He sang it on the talent show The Rap of China in summer 2019; he was eliminated, but the song blew up online. On Douyin the big trend was a hand dance in which people follow the song's spoken cues to trace a dragon and a rainbow in the air. Full of northeastern humor and 1990s disco nostalgia, it was even reworked as 过年disco (New Year Disco) for the 2020 CCTV Spring Festival Gala.

body: The lyrics were written for crowd interaction, so almost every line works as a dance cue. On Douyin people sway to the beat and use their hands to draw circles and waves in front of their bodies, tracing a "dragon" and a "rainbow", a routine nicknamed 画龙舞 (the dragon-drawing dance). It is easy enough for one person in front of a phone or a whole square-dance group.

The song's hero, 老舅 ("little uncle"), is the youngest son of a northeastern family, in a leather jacket and slicked-back hair with a pager on his belt, taking you out to the disco. That lovably dated image made people laugh, and 宝石老舅 (Uncle Gem) became the singer's nickname.

Event

He performs it in the revival round of The Rap of China season 2, and it starts spreading online
野狼disco is released digitally; the dragon-drawing dance floods Douyin and celebrities join in
A version with Hong Kong singer William Chan (陈伟霆) is released, widening its reach
At the CCTV Spring Festival Gala, Gem, Lay Zhang and William Chan perform the reworked 过年disco

body: The title comes from 野狼王 Disco, a series of 1990s dance-music compilations that many people in northeast China remember from discos and video halls. Gem used the name to call up those nights out, then layered northeastern-dialect rap over retro electronic beats. "Wild wolf" sounds rough and gloriously tacky, exactly the mood the song is after.

ul: The lyrics come with built-in moves, so anyone can copy the dance after one listen
The northeastern accent and the "little uncle" character are funny and nostalgic for people born in the 1980s and 1990s
The hook is relentlessly catchy; reports put total plays across platforms above one billion
Celebrity covers and the Spring Festival Gala version took it from internet hit to the mainstream

faq.a: 宝石Gem (Gem, real name Dong Baoshi), a rapper from Changchun who also wrote the words and music. He later released a version with Hong Kong singer William Chan (陈伟霆).

faq.q: How do you do the 野狼disco dance on Douyin?
faq.a: Sway side to side on the beat and follow the song's cues with your hands, drawing circles and waves in front of you to trace a dragon and then a rainbow. That is the "dragon-drawing dance".
"Wild Wolf Disco". The name comes from 野狼王 Disco, a 1990s dance-music compilation series, and stands for northeast China's old disco nights, not an actual wolf.
